builds.name: Reference: Ranked jungle core
builds.goal: Reference for Rengar: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ jungle players use most (7,377 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 52.8% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: An ambush fighter who leaps from brush or camouflage, builds Ferocity and chooses empowered damage, healing-cleanse or root. The current jungle provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Umbral Glaive → Profane Hydra → Lord Dominik's Regards. Fleet Footwork keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Ionian Boots of Lucidity, Edge of Night, Infinity Edge.
builds.summary: The proven jungle baseline: Umbral Glaive → Profane Hydra → Lord Dominik's Regards, with Fleet Footwork.
testPlan: Play it in jungle as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Umbral Glaive → Profane Hydra → Lord Dominik's Regards) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 52.8% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Umbral Glaive → Profane Hydra → Lord Dominik's Regards.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.

builds.name: Double-roar AP retreat
builds.summary: Test normal and empowered W damage with recovery after taking a finite burst.
builds.goal: Test normal and empowered W damage with recovery after taking a finite burst.
builds.hypothesis: W has 0.8 AP magic damage and restores half of damage received in the last 1.5 seconds; empowered W adds a cleanse. AP and magic penetration target those roars while Visage improves received healing. Passive ferocity and E control must enable the actual empowered W, trading away empowered Q damage.
testPlan: Required state: Record initial ferocity, burst taken and both W timings within the recovery window.
Measure W packets and heal amounts with controlled incoming burst and finite ferocity.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: No recent incoming damage means little W recovery; AP reduces the AD leap threat.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Empowered W cleanse does not justify inventing additional healing beyond the recorded W behavior.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Hextech Rocketbelt, Riftmaker, Void Staff, Zhonya's Hourglass, Spirit Visage, Sorcerer's Shoes. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Physical matchup
builds.goal: Situational adaptation for Rengar: adapt to the specified fight rather than assume one universal build
builds.hypothesis: An ambush fighter who leaps from brush or camouflage, builds Ferocity and chooses empowered damage, healing-cleanse or root. Fix Ferocity and brush/ultimate entry, then choose empowered Q/W/E. Do not claim empowered heal/cleanse and damage from the same four-stack resource at once. Armor and access may turn survival into additional attack/spell windows.
builds.summary: Armor and access may turn survival into additional attack/spell windows.
testPlan: Kit question for Rengar: Fix Ferocity and brush/ultimate entry, then choose empowered Q/W/E. Do not claim empowered heal/cleanse and damage from the same four-stack resource at once.

Start with the early core (Stridebreaker, then matchup armor) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Compare against the reference route at the same level, gold spent, finite stacks and opponent setup. Record unused gold; isolate an item change before changing runes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Resource: Ferocity. Do not treat mana regeneration as Ferocity recovery; Nimbus replaces Manaflow when that Sorcery row is used.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: Armor and access may turn survival into additional attack/spell windows. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern. Choose the opponent profile this defensive route is intended to address, then repeat against the wrong damage type.

Q evidence: Rengar's next Attack brutally stabs his target for bonus damage.

Ferocity effect: deals increased damage and grants Attack Speed. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: Randuin is conditional on the enemy attack/crit profile; it costs an offensive slot.

The route fails Rengar's stated kit question: Fix Ferocity and brush/ultimate entry, then choose empowered Q/W/E. Do not claim empowered heal/cleanse and damage from the same four-stack resource at once.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: Randuin is conditional on the enemy attack/crit profile; it costs an offensive slot.
Full cost 16,100 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
Counter-items are conditional. Change boots/defense for the real matchup, then record the modified setup.
buyOrder: Stridebreaker, then matchup armor. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Randuin's Omen, Spirit Visage, Sterak's Gage are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Resource: Ferocity. Do not treat mana regeneration as Ferocity recovery; Nimbus replaces Manaflow when that Sorcery row is used.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

builds.name: Ferocity recovery chase
builds.summary: Use empowered-cast speed to keep healing attack trades within reach.
builds.goal: Use empowered-cast speed to keep healing attack trades within reach.
builds.hypothesis: Passive grants brief speed after an empowered ability; Q gives the next two attacks attack speed. Sundered Sky and Ravenous support real attacks while Visage improves W and item healing. Trinity adds one Spellblade packet; normal/empowered E can constrain an escape before choosing healing W or damage Q.
testPlan: Required state: Brush/leap access and a finite four-ferocity cycle permit more than the opening hit.
Compare damage and health retained over two ferocity cycles, tracking which empowered spell was chosen.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: No brush, healing reduction or forced disengage leaves an inferior burst sequence.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Q first-attack scaling is not proof every Q bonus inherits ordinary critical multipliers.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
